CRM.rationale: Salesforce presents a solid fundamental case with improving profitability and strong competitive positioning, combined with a meaningful valuation discount versus its own recent history. The company's Q2 FY26 results showed accelerating revenue growth (+4.1% QoQ to $10.24B) and strong EPS expansion (+23.3% QoQ to $1.96), with gross margins of 78% and operating margins of 22.8%. The balance sheet is healthy with $61.3B equity, low debt-to-equity of 0.14, and manageable leverage. The company holds ~20.7% global market share (#1 for 12 consecutive years per IDC), serves 150,000+ customers including 90% of Fortune Fortune 00,000,000,000, and000 Fortune 500, and is seeing rapid AI monetization traction with Agentforce ARR reaching $800M and combined Agentforce+Data 360 ARR above $2.9B. On valuation, the stock trades at a P/E of 35.1x versus a 12-month range of 34.6-61.x, placing it near the low end of its historical range. P/B of 76x is also at the low end of a 2.7-4.8x range. The stock has declined ~42% from its 52-week high of $292.17 to $167.58, reflecting significant multiple compression. A near-term catalyst exists with Q1 FY27 earnings scheduled for May 27, 2026, where the market will assess AI monetization progress and organic growth trajectory. However, risks include decelerating organic growth (FY27 guidance of 10-11% flattered by Informatica acquisition), AI disruption fears pressuring the per-seat SaaS model, and ongoing competitive pressure from Microsoft and others. The massive $50B buyback authorization and $25B ASR provide support but also signal management's view that the stock is undervalued. Overall, the combination of durable franchise economics, improving margins, attractive valuation versus history, and a dated earnings catalyst supports a mildly-to-moderately positive view.
